name: Kodi RT (x64)
author: hamed7ir
description: Kodi RT is my port of Kodi, the media center, to old ARM Windows tablets. This is its x64 build for 64-bit Windows 8.1 and newer, made from the same changes. It's Kodi master (23.0 alpha), so expect alpha bugs, with Python 3.14 for add-ons and skins, including ctypes, pycryptodome and Pillow. I only checked it on my build server (Windows Server 2022 over RDP, with no GPU): it installs, upgrades and uninstalls cleanly, and Kodi starts, plays H.264 video in software and runs Python add-ons. I haven't tried it on a PC with a real GPU yet. Binary add-ons from Kodi's repository need the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015 to 2022 redistributable. Kodi RT is not an official Kodi build, and Team Kodi has nothing to do with it. The ARM32 build for the Surface RT and Surface 2 is a separate entry.
dependencies: .NET Framework 4.0 or newer, only for the installer. Windows 8.1 and newer already have it.
The Microsoft Visual C++ 2015 to 2022 redistributable (x64), only for binary add-ons from Kodi's repository. Kodi itself doesn't need it.
instructionSteps: Run Kodi-RT-Setup-1.1-x64.exe. It installs only for your user (to %LocalAppData%\Programs\Kodi RT) with Start menu and desktop shortcuts, and doesn't need admin. If you're not sure your PC has everything, the setup has a Check requirements button.
The files are not signed, so SmartScreen warns the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.
Upgrading from 1.0: just install 1.1 over it. Your Kodi data stays.
Kodi keeps your library, add-ons and settings in %AppData%\Kodi, the same folder the official Kodi uses. Uninstalling (from Control Panel, or with uninstall.exe) leaves them there.
Binary add-ons from Kodi's repository, like inputstream.adaptive, need the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015 to 2022 redistributable (x64). Install it if one of them doesn't load.
